Original Requirements: The Sun Search Control System (SSCS) manages satellite attitude acquisition and maintenance using gyroscopes, sun sensors, and thrusters. It operates on an 80C32 microcontroller with a 32ms interrupt cycle and 160ms control cycle. Key functions include rate damping, pitch/roll sun search, sun cruising, fault management (gyro communication, thruster firing), and telemetry transmission via serial ports.
Product Goals: Ensure precise satellite attitude control and sun acquisition within hardware constraints
Guarantee system reliability through robust fault detection and recovery mechanisms
Maintain real-time performance with strict 32ms interrupt and 160ms cycle timing
User Stories: As a Ground Operator, I want to send mode commands via serial port to control the satellite's operating state
As the System, I need to automatically switch to a backup sun sensor if the primary fails to detect sunlight after two search attempts
As the System, I need to stabilize three-axis angular velocity to zero during rate damping mode to ensure attitude stability
As a Ground Operator, I want to receive packaged telemetry data every 160ms to monitor satellite status in real-time
As the System, I need to halt thruster operations if frequent firing faults are detected to prevent fuel waste and hardware damage
Competitive Analysis: Standard PID ACS: Common architecture but lacks specific sun-search state machine logic
AI-based ACS: High computational requirement, incompatible with 80C32 constraints
Redundant Hardware ACS: Higher reliability but increased cost and weight
Legacy SSCS Version: Existing codebase but lacks updated fault management protocols
COTS ACS Solution: Less customizable for specific sun-search maneuver requirements
FPGA-based ACS: Higher speed but excessive power consumption for this mission profile
Custom 80C32 SSCS (Target): Optimized for specific mission constraints and cost-efficiency

Requirement Analysis: The system requires a main program plus interrupt architecture on an 80C32 CPU. Critical timing constraints include a 32ms timer interrupt (GTCR0 0x8083) and a 160ms control cycle. Communication involves multiple serial ports (0x881, 0x881A, 0x88DA, 0x88DB) with strict byte interval timing (<5us). The control logic must handle four modes (RDSM, PASM, RASM, CSM) and manage hardware interfaces for 9 gyros, 4 sun sensors, and 12 thrusters. Fault management is critical, requiring detection of gyro communication errors (5 consecutive cycles) and thruster frequent firing (<1s interval for 5s). Telemetry must be packaged and transmitted asynchronously.
Requirement Pool: Implement 32ms timer interrupt and 160ms control cycle timing logic
Develop attitude control algorithms for Rate Damping, Pitch Search, Roll Search, and Sun Cruise modes
Implement fault management for gyro communication errors and thruster frequent firing
Establish serial communication protocols for ground commands and telemetry (0x88DA, 0x88DB)
Implement sun sensor switching logic and backup sensor activation
UI Design draft: No traditional GUI. Ground Station Interface will display telemetry data including Current Mode Word, Three-axis Angular Velocity, Sun Visibility Flag, and Sensor Angles. Data format is binary/telemetry stream decoded for text display. Digital tube display on hardware for basic status codes.
